Shlok Koirala is an AI Engineer focused on production machine learning systems, LLM pipelines, and multilingual NLP for low-resource languages. His work spans retrieval-augmented generation, multi-agent systems, computer vision, and computational linguistics.

At Perceive Now, he architected a production RAG report generation system using LangChain, ChromaDB, and the OpenAI API. The system automated enterprise market research across Healthcare, CPG, Supply Chain, and Construction, reducing manual research effort by 80 percent. He also engineered multi-agent systems that reduced traditional research processing time by 30 percent and delivered more than 20 third-party platform integrations.

At AISSR Lab at Kathmandu University, he conducted applied AI research in generative AI and computer vision for agriculture, heritage conservation, and human-wildlife conflict resolution. His research on heritage restoration became Shades of History, a live Hugging Face image colorization demo and a publication in the Journal of NAST College.

Sanjyaan is an AI learning assistant for students with dysgraphia and dyscalculia. It uses personalized learning workflows, adaptive LLM content delivery, real-time feedback, and assistive interaction modes for Nepali educational contexts. The project won Hackedemia 2.0 in 2024 among more than 100 competing teams.

Abstractive QA is a multilingual Nepali question-answering system fine-tuned with MuRIL-large on a custom dataset. The pipeline uses sliding-window tokenization, span extraction, offset mapping, n-best answer scoring, mixed-precision training, and gradient accumulation.

ChandaParser is a computational linguistics engine for Sanskrit and Nepali poetic meter. It uses Devanagari-aware syllabification, Chandahashastra rules, all eight Ganas, Laghu and Guru syllable weighting, and Levenshtein matching to identify more than 20 classical meters.
